lessons.title: ળ (ḷa) — one new shape, retroflex lla

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write retroflex nna once from memory. Keep the tongue-curl idea, but put the old shape away: today it receives a different sound and form.

Keep ળ (ḷa) visible. It is retroflex lla: the tongue curls back for the l sound. Begin at the upper left and circle the broad left bowl. Continue upward through the narrow middle turn, cross the high right arch, and descend the tall spine into its lower foot without lifting.
Finger-trace ળ (ḷa) once, then air-trace it once. Notice broad bowl, narrow turn, high arch, tall spine; no pen lift.
Copy visible ળ (ḷa) once. Compare only the broad bowl and tall spine; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write retroflex lla once. Uncover ળ (ḷa), compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write retroflex lla from memory.

feedback.correct: ળ — the broad bowl and tall spine are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at ળ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Name the sound, the two main landmarks, and the pen-lift count.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write retroflex lla once from memory. Check only its broad bowl and tall spine.

Keep થ visible. It is tha: say ta with a clear puff of air. Begin at the right of the small upper loop, circle it, descend through the middle, and sweep around the broad lower body into the right shoulder. Lift once; descend the tall right spine and turn through its lower foot.
Finger-trace થ (tha) once, then air-trace it once. Notice small upper loop, broad lower body, separate right spine; one pen lift.
Copy visible થ (tha) once. Compare only the upper loop and separate spine; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write tha once. Uncover થ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write aspirated tha from memory.

feedback.correct: થ — the upper loop, lower body, and separate spine are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at થ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Say tha with its puff, then name the pen-lift count.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write tha once from memory. Then say the vowel already carried by a bare Gujarati consonant: short a.

Keep અ visible. It is independent short a, used when the vowel begins a syllable without a consonant. Sweep clockwise around the open left curve, continue through the lower body, rise into the middle shoulder, and finish the small right arch. Lift once; descend the separate right stem into its foot.
Finger-trace અ once, then air-trace it once. Notice open left curve, middle shoulder, small arch, separate right stem; one pen lift.
Copy visible અ once. Compare only the open curve and separate stem; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write independent short a once. Uncover અ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write independent short a from memory.

feedback.correct: અ — short a is standing as its own letter.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at અ, hide it, and repair only the open curve or separate stem.

segments.text: When does short a need અ instead of arriving free on a consonant? (When it stands without a consonant.)
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

lessons.title: િ (-i) — short i sits before, sounds after

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Point to અ and શ. Say independent short a, then sha. Do not combine them; today one small sign changes only the vowel on શ.

Keep િ visible. It is the attached short-i sign. It is written to the left of its consonant even though i is pronounced after that consonant. With શ, it makes શિ, shi. Start with the upright stem and finish through the curl that reaches toward the consonant.
Finger-trace િ (-i) once, then air-trace it once. Notice the sign's left-side place in શિ. Say shi only after the whole form is visible.
Copy visible શિ once. Circle only the short-i sign and check that it sits to the left of શ; repair its placement once if needed.
Hide the model. Add short i to શ and write shi. Uncover શિ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model. Add short i to શ and write shi.

feedback.correct: શિ — the sign is seen before શ and pronounced after it.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at શિ, hide it, and repair only the short-i sign's placement.

segments.text: Is િ (-i) seen before or after its consonant? (Before.) Is it pronounced before or after? (After.)
Source: Unicode Gujarati chart; placement and example follow data/scripts/gujarati.json.

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Keep the four cards visible. Point as you say retroflex lla, aspirated tha, independent short a, and attached short i. For િ (-i), also say: seen before, heard after.
Read the row once from left to right. Give િ (-i) its role as an attached sign, not as an independent letter. Record a reading score out of four.

segments.prompt: Read these four forms aloud in order: ળ (ḷa) થ (tha) અ િ (-i).
acceptedResponses: retroflex lla; aspirated tha; independent short a; attached short i

feedback.incorrect: Name only the missed form, compare one landmark, then read the row again.

segments.text: Cover every model. Write the four cues in order. Record a separate writing score out of four; a reading point cannot replace a written form. Aim for 4/4 in each column, with one focused repair allowed.

segments.prompt: Cover every model. Write from these cues: retroflex lla, aspirated tha, independent short a, attached short i.

feedback.correct: The four forms returned without a visible model.
feedback.incorrect: Uncover only the missed form, repair one landmark, cover it, and retry once.

segments.text: Write the only attached sign in the row, then say its placement rule.
